title: Software modification - Vaporize Windows Swift path survival

stateResults.summary: The operator directed path shortening as a prerequisite for making Swift reliable on Windows and rejected unowned scratch leakage.
The canonical standalone Vaporize repository was clean before implementation.
Admitted a typed Windows SwiftPM path-budget plan, conditionally selected a short deterministic scratch path, preserved explicit overrides, and bound the behavior to CUJ-01.
swift test --filter WindowsSwiftPMPathPolicyTests passed 6 tests in one suite on x86_64 Windows. SwiftPM refreshed Package.resolved to the graph exercised by that build.

Vaporize now warns after Windows CLI installs when .swiftpm/bin is absent from the user PATH and exposes an explicit idempotent path add-swiftpm-bin command. The command preserves unrelated entries, recognizes equivalent %USERPROFILE% spellings, updates only the current user's PATH, and verifies the persisted write. The focused Windows CUJ passed 9 of 9 tests in an isolated short scratch path while an unrelated WCode process held the default debug executable open.

Vaporize now exposes path add-swiftpm-bin on every platform and delegates inspection and mutation to SwiftCLIInstaller. The embedded PowerShell source and feature-local Windows conditionals were removed. CUJ-01 passed 7 tests on x86_64 Windows, and the built command verified the existing Windows user PATH idempotently through reg.exe.
Persist only after executable Windows evidence is green.

receiptRefs.t: Windows SwiftPM path-survival CUJ and focused test

notes: The observed Git/SwiftPM path failure and the later DocC archive failure are separate defects and remain separately classified.
Scratch leasing, quota enforcement, expiry, cleanup, and pressure notification are the next bounded product slice.
